CRIMINAL CASE No. 52453 of 2024  RINKU MOURYA  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
Mr. Sarvesh Kumar Sharma - Advocate for the applican  Mr. Rajendra Singh Yadav - Public Prosecutor for res  State.
Mr. Pramod Pachouri - Advocate for respondent No. 2

ORDER This is third application filed by the applicant under Section 482 of B.N.S.S. / 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail relating to Crime No. 482/2023 registered at Police Station - Dabra,
District - Gwalior (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376 and 506 of IPC.
Earlier applications were dismissed as withdrawn.
Learned counsel for the applicant / accused argued that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
After withdrawal of second anticipatory bail application, DNA report has been received which has come negative in respect to present applicant.

It is further argued that in the first statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. on 09.6.2023, no allegation was levelled by her against the applicant, however, in her second statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. on 14.6.2023, she made allegations of rape against the applicant.

Under these circumstances,
entire prosecution story becomes doubtful.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22097 2 MCRC-52453-2024
It is further argued that applicant is the reputed citizen of the society and in case he is sent to jail, his reputation would get diminished.
Further argument is that applicant is the permanent resident of District - Gwalior (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconding or tampering with the prosecution evidence.

sentences.text: Hence, prayed for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the prosecutrix vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application and argued that in the FIR as well as in the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., specific allegation of rape has been levelled against the applicant, therefore, looking to the nature of offence, anticipatory bail application of the applicant be rejected.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary.
It would not be desirable to enter into merits of the rival contentions at this juncture.
It is well settled that the considerations governing grant of anticipatory bail are altogether different from those relevant for the prayer for regular bail.

Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, looking to the nature of allegation levelled against the applicant and manner in which he is involved in the offence, as alleged by the prosecution, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.
Consequently, the present bail application is hereby dismissed.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE AKS Rinku Mourya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11418770/
